summary.oneLiner: Trident Limited is one of India's leading vertically integrated manufacturers of yarn, bed and bath linen, paper and chemicals, and is the flagship company of the Trident group.
summary.business: Trident operates diversified business segments comprising Bed Linen, Bath Linen, Yarn, Paper and Chemicals, supported by a captive power plant that meets the internal power needs of its various business segments. It runs an integrated fibre-to-fabric textile ecosystem alongside a sustainable paper operation that makes high-speed printing and publishing paper, branded copier paper and wheat straw-based paper. The Company serves leading global retailers, brands, hospitality players, institutional buyers, printing and publishing customers and e-commerce platforms across more than 100 countries, …

It runs an integrated fibre-to-fabric textile ecosystem alongside a sustainable paper operation that makes high-speed printing and publishing paper, branded copier paper and wheat straw-based paper. The Company serves leading global retailers, brands, hospitality players, institutional buyers, printing and publishing customers and e-commerce platforms across more than 100 countries, in both branded and private-label formats.

currentContext.expansion: The only specific expansion disclosed in the routed sections is in the Directors' Report under 'Expansions/Modernisation': during FY2025-26 the Company expanded its captive solar power capacity by 5.40 MWp, taking total installed captive solar power capacity to 57.38 MWp, framed as part of its commitment to reducing its carbon footprint and adopting environmentally responsible energy solutions. There was no change in share capital during the year. Beyond this, expansion intent is stated only qualitatively: the Chairman Emeritus describes a phase of 'fundamental reinvention' involving aggressive investment in modernisation, automation, digital transformation and Artificial Intelligence, expanding capabilities through new technologies, innovative products and new market opportunities, strengthening domestic presence and brand building, and accelerating the commitment to renewable energy; the Corporate Overview lists building future-ready manufacturing capabilities through automation and digitalisation, diversifying into high-value and sustainable product segments, and deepening presence across global markets and the domestic retail/e-commerce ecosystem; and the Managing Director describes accelerated Industry 4.0 adoption with real-time monitoring, smart manufacturing systems and advanced analytics, with AI-driven projects being integrated under the 'Digital Trident' agenda. No plant-level capacity addition project, commissioning timeline, site-wise capex plan or rupee capex outlay is disclosed in these sections.

risks.note: A significant share of revenue remains linked to global demand conditions and trade policies — exports contributed 53.73% of total sale in FY2025-26, so weakness in overseas retail demand or adverse tariff action transmits directly to the top line.

Global conflicts, shipping disruptions and changes in international trade policies may impact exports, supply chains and export competitiveness; management flagged trade barriers, geopolitical developments and supply-chain disruptions across several markets during the year.
Fluctuations in cotton, pulp, fuel chemicals and energy prices can affect margins; freight rate volatility and shipping disruptions can further impact costs and delivery timelines.

Operations in textiles and paper are energy-intensive and dependent on conventional energy sources; failure to mitigate Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions could expose the Company to carbon pricing mechanisms, carbon taxes and stricter emission reporting obligations, while India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) may raise compliance costs.

risks.risk: Physical climate risk and cotton raw-material availability
risks.note: Manufacturing facilities are directly exposed to extreme heat waves, flooding and water scarcity that can disrupt plant operations and damage infrastructure; dependence on cotton as a primary raw material presents supply risk as erratic rainfall, prolonged droughts and rising temperatures drive up procurement costs.

Sustained investments are required for technology upgrades, sustainability initiatives and capacity enhancement, while textile and paper operations consume significant energy, water and raw materials — exposing the Company to both reinvestment burden and evolving environmental compliance costs.
Competition from low-cost manufacturing nations may exert pricing pressure on Trident's export-facing textile businesses.

risks.risk: Dependence on skilled workforce and attrition
risks.note: Large-scale manufacturing operations require continuous availability of skilled and technical talent; the turnover rate for permanent employees was 38.77% in FY2025-26 (40.57% in FY2024-25) and for permanent workers 22.23%.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
